output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes mainly from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency staff. The move silently dropped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. These included the 15-second hold-off for brief oxygen dips, suppression of repeat alerts, and routing of probe-off alarms to the charge phone only. Phone notifications per nurse roughly doubled in Pods A-C and acknowledgement time doubled. Pod D, still on the old server, saw no change. Within Pods A-C, core and agency nurses did equally badly, so staffing mix does not explain it. Monitor alarm volume was flat, which counts against heavier patient acuity and the September monitor update as causes. Sick leave rising is plausibly partly the virus season; a link to alert load is unproven. I'm fairly confident. Next step: restore the old rules (about 4 hours plus clinical validation), with Clinical Engineering and the alarm committee signing off. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Don't cap agency use or open performance reviews; they would punish the wrong people. Don't stop phone forwarding of alarms. Wireless coverage at Room 14 is worth a quick check later.
